messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Urgent fix needed before year-end surge",
 "problem_statement": "Customers face delays in resolving critical issues just before a high-volume claims period. Without timely fixes, operations risk disruption during peak demand.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "We need this fixed before the year-end claims surge.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-31T11:19:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the sole quote from support on 2026-10-31, 'We need this fixed before the year-end claims surge.' Neither the title, problem statement, nor the quote identifies what the actual product defect is; there is only a demand for a fix and timing urgency, with no described bug, missing capability, workaround, or product behavior a squad could act on. Without a concrete product problem, this is not actionable signal.", "verdict": "fail"}
